34 A circuit needs to be completed by connecting two resistors between points X and Y, as shown.
The resistors can be connected in series or in parallel with each other.

Which combination of resistors produces the least resistance between X and Y?

hints: Notice the table asks you to compare $20\,\Omega$ with $40\,\Omega$ against $40\,\Omega$ with $100\,\Omega$, each in series and in parallel between X and Y.
Recall that series adds as $R = R_1 + R_2$ while parallel adds as $1/R = 1/R_1 + 1/R_2$, so any parallel value is less than either series value and less than the smallest single resistor.
Calculate the two parallel values with $R = R_1 R_2/(R_1+R_2)$ and check which pair of smaller resistors gives the smaller result.
walkthrough: Identify the rules: for series $R_{total} = R_1 + R_2$, and for parallel $1/R_{total} = 1/R_1 + 1/R_2$ or $R_{total} = R_1R_2/(R_1+R_2)$.
Compare all four: $13.3\,\Omega < 28.6\,\Omega < 60\,\Omega < 140\,\Omega$, so parallel always beats series and the smaller pair in parallel beats the larger pair in parallel.
The least resistance is therefore $20\,\Omega$ and $40\,\Omega$ in parallel. This is option A.

A.explanation: Parallel of $20\,\Omega$ and $40\,\Omega$ gives about $13.3\,\Omega$, smaller than the smallest resistor and the least of the four.

B.explanation: Parallel of $40\,\Omega$ and $100\,\Omega$ gives about $28.6\,\Omega$, which is larger than the $20\,\Omega$ and $40\,\Omega$ parallel value.

C.explanation: Series of $20\,\Omega$ and $40\,\Omega$ gives $60\,\Omega$, much larger than either parallel combination.

D.explanation: Series of $40\,\Omega$ and $100\,\Omega$ gives $140\,\Omega$, the largest resistance of the four.
